https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c980.text: Figure caption, Watch: Trump tells reporters why he switched planes By Sareen Habeshian Published 12 August 2026, 02:50 BST Updated 3 hours ago President Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month due to a possible threat. "I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go in a different flight, different plane," Trump told reporters. "I just have to do what they say." The revelation comes after reports that Trump boarded Air Force One on 8 July in view of television cameras, before hiding in a catering truck to be transported to a military aircraft. The last-minute switch has raised questions about whether those left on the decoy plane were in danger, but Trump said on Tuesday the jet he boarded instead could have been at "greater risk... because that would be the plane, I think, that they would be more likely to go for." Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The New York Times reported that US intelligence had information of a person near the Nato summit who had been seen with a shoulder-fired missile. Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know the US president had been smuggled out as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat. Figure caption, Watch: Was Donald Trump smuggled out of Air Force One in a catering truck? Trump has previously said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara. "I guess there was a threat out there," the president said during a visit aboard Air Force One to an event in Ohio on Tuesday. "I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats." He added: "I have a lot of threats that you don't know about." The clandestine manoeuvre last month came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war. Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake". On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he slipped off Air Force One on to a catering truck that had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded. He was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper. Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board. A media pool producer who was on the plane said they found it unusual when they were told to keep the window shades down. A photographer briefly opened a shade and reportedly was quickly told to close it. The producer's comments were detailed in a report from the White House Correspondents' Association on Tuesday. They also noted there appeared to have been two catering trucks at both the front and back of the plane when the press arrived, and that the media van had been too far back in the motorcade at the airport be able to take a photo of the president boarding. Figure caption, Watch: Washington Post and AP reporters reveal details of plane swap over Iran threat Technically "Air Force One" is the call sign for any aircraft carrying the US president. But on this occasion, the C-32A used the call sign "Reach 18", while the aircraft carrying the journalists continued to use "AF1" in order to keep up the ruse. Remaining on the original aircraft were members of Trump's cabinet, according to the New York Times. The outlet, citing two anonymous officials, reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were on board. Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall. It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet. Trump's dramatic plane swap hints at personal stakes of Iran war Published 7 hours ago Inside the Secret Service 'shell game' to hide US presidents in plain sight Published 10 hours ago The president then transferred to the new Qatari-donated Air Force One to travel back to Washington. During that flight, Trump spoke to reporters on board where he noted the threats posed by Iran but did not mention the earlier plane swap. Asked why reporters had been told to lower the window shades on the plane from Turkey, Trump said at the time: "Because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags we have to deal with." He said he had a "threat all the time" on his life, and that he is "number one" on Iran's "list". Jose Zamora, regional director for the Americas for the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a statement that the Trump administration "has a responsibility to ensure that journalists covering the president are not unnecessarily exposed to danger". "Reporters should be informed of credible security threats so they can make informed decisions about their safety," he added. Skip next section Rahul Gandhi's key petition on mass voter deletions listed in Supreme Court today Published 10/15/2026 Published October 15, 2026 last updated 10/15/2026 last updated October 15, 2026 Rahul Gandhi's key petition on mass voter deletions listed in Supreme Court today The Supreme Court is slated to hear a petition filed by India's main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition lawmakers over a sweeping exercise which has so far purged over 130 million names from the country's electoral rolls. A list of cases to be taken up on Thursday by a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant shows the petition named "Rahul Gandhi and others versus Election Commission of India and others." The plea was filed on Monday at the end of a protest march to the Supreme Court that saw Congress' Gandhi rallying thousands, including members of the opposition INDIA bloc, student leaders, activists and civil society, through a heavily barricaded part of the capital. The protest was the latest in a series of demonstrations calling for India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down over alleged manipulation of voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The poll body, whose neutrality has come under scrutiny, rejects the allegations and says the exercise, called Special Intensive Revision (SIR), removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and also prevents the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants." Modi's party has also dismissed the accusations and deems the protests as attempts to "create anarchy." Meanwhile, neither Modi nor Kumar have publicly addressed the issue. Gandhi's petition seeks an interim suspension of the nationwide revision of voter rolls, along with an audit of voter deletions and safeguards against deletions without prior notice. https://p.dw.com/p/5OGYJ Skip next section India expected to overtake Japan as 4th largest economy in 2027 — IMF 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 India expected to overtake Japan as 4th largest economy in 2027 — IMF India is expected to overtake Japan to become the fourth-largest economy in the world by next year, according to projections released by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday. The Washington-based organization said that while this year Japan would continue to hold its spot as the fourth-largest nation by nominal gross domestic product, India was set to take over with a GDP estimated at $4.52 trillion (€4.03 trillion) in 2027. The projection showed Japan sliding to sixth place next year, ranking behind India and the United Kingdom. The United States leads as the world's largest economy, followed by China and Germany. The IMF's Asia and Pacific Department Director Krishna Srinivasan said India entered the ongoing energy price shock caused by the Middle East conflict from a strong position. "Growth was strong, fiscal prudence was pretty much enshrined, they had lots of reserves and so on," he said. "And so in that context, they have responded well to the shock." https://p.dw.com/p/5OHBa Skip next section Supreme Court seeks response from Election Commission to Rahul Gandhi's plea 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 Supreme Court seeks response from Election Commission to Rahul Gandhi's plea The Supreme Court has issued a notice to the Election Commission of India and the body's three commissioners, including top official Gyanesh Kumar, seeking their response over a petition filed by Congress' Rahul Gandhi. The opposition leader and other lawmakers had filed the petition over alleged irregularities in a widespread revision of the country's electoral rolls. The court said it would group the petition together with several pending pleas related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists. "We are issuing notice and tagging it with the matters already pending. Somebody will accept notice on behalf of the Election Commission of India. Otherwise, serve them," legal news website Bar and Bench cited the top court as saying. Gandhi and leaders of the INDIA bloc of opposition parties filed the plea on October 12, following a massive protest march to the Supreme Court. The protest was among a flurry of demonstrations that the nation has witnessed in recent weeks, calling for Kumar's resignation. It came after a newspaper investigation found Kumar allegedly took unilateral decisions that resulted in a mass deletion of voters, allegedly violating the law. The Indian Express reported that two of Kumar's fellow election commissioners raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months regarding voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral roll data but those concerns were not taken into consideration. On Thursday, the Supreme Court also issued a notice in another plea to Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protesters over their Monday march to its complex. Khan, who is a US national, was briefly detained during the protest against alleged voter roll manipulation held at August Kranti Maidan in Maharashtra's Mumbai city on Saturday. Khan had posted a picture of himself on Instagram from inside a police van. "Apparently I'm going for a drive," he said in the post. Videos of him being pulled inside the van by police officials subsequently went viral on social media. The notice directs Khan to leave India by October 28 for allegedly violating provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, reports said. The vice president of Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) Maharashtra unit, Kirit Somaiya, had earlier called for Khan to be arrested and deported over alleged violations of Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) provisions and visa norms. Speaking to the media before he was detained on Saturday, Khan said that he had come to the protest location as a citizen of Mumbai and was not there with any specific demands. "I don't have demands. I am here as a citizen, as a person who lives in this city. I am here to see why freedom of movement is being restricted. Why are people's voices being suppressed? That is why I am here," he said. Khan is the nephew of prominent Bollywood actor Aamir Khan. https://p.dw.com/p/5OGot Skip next section Three Indians killed in Germany building fire, arson suspected 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 Three Indians killed in Germany building fire, arson suspected Three Indian nationals were killed in a fire at an apartment building in western Germany's Bochum. The Indian Embassy in Berlin said in a statement that two women and one man were among those who died, adding that all three were studying in Germany. According to German media reports, the victims were aged between 25 and 27. Five other people were injured. German news agency DPA said that the fire department received an alert at 4:15 a.m. local time (0212 GMT/UTC). Residents were seen calling for help as they stood at windows on the first and second floors of the building, DPA reported. The firefighting efforts lasted several hours. A technical malfunction was ruled out as the cause of the fire and authorities said they were investigating a suspected arson. A 41-year-old man, who is a resident of the building, has been arrested on suspicion of murder and is in pretrial detention, reports said citing a police statement. The reports identified the man as a Romanian national. Meanwhile, the Indian Embassy said it was in touch with German authorities and the families of the victims. It added that it was offering all necessary assistance. "We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief," the statement from the embassy said. Bochum's mayor, Jörg Lukat, called the incident a "tragedy the likes of which Bochum has not seen in decades." https://p.dw.com/p/5OGlQ Skip next section India's top diplomat in UAE for talks 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 India's top diplomat in UAE for talks Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar has met United Arab Emirates' Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan while on a visit to Abu Dhabi. Jaishankar called the meeting "warm and productive" in a post on X and said that the two sides discussed bilateral and global issues. The Indian top diplomat's three-day visit to the UAE began on Wednesday. A statement released by the Foreign Ministry in New Delhi earlier this week said the bilateral talks would review the progress of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and the UAE. Jaishankar is also taking part in the Raisina Middle East forum in Abu Dhabi, co-hosted by New Delhi-based think tank Observer Research Foundation and the foreign ministries of India and the UAE. He said a discussion with Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan at the event underpinned the importance of recognizing the increasing pace of change in the global order, highlighting that it reflects "long term trends and immediate shocks." "Countries respond as per their specific situation. New partnerships and fresh options are inevitably explored in that pursuit," he said, adding that it involved going beyond "traditional comfort zones and developing sharper strategic awareness." Jaishankar also called for an urgent "reform of multilateralism," which he said could be supported through a more robust "minilateralism." https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/142193.text: NATO commander urges Canada to invest in drones and AI to strengthen military The Canadian government has also launched a Defence Drone Initiative to expand drone capabilities A senior NATO commander has urged Canada to invest in artificial intelligence and advanced military drones as the country prepares to increase defence spending by billions of dollars. Speaking to Global News from Latvia, Admiral Pierre Vandier, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, said modern militaries must combine new technologies with traditional weapons and equipment. “A force that is not protected against drones and (drone) swarms is a force at risk,” Vandier said. His comments followed NATO military exercises in Latvia, where forces tested drones, electronic warfare and AI technology alongside conventional ground operations. The exercises examined how new technologies could improve military effectiveness and protect troops against emerging threats. “What we demonstrated was we can extend lethality and extend survivability of existing capabilities … if we bring them with a good mix of new technology,” Vandier said. Canada currently has around 3,000 military personnel stationed in Latvia under Operation Reassurance, NATO's mission to strengthen security in eastern Europe. The Canadian government has also launched a Defence Drone Initiative to expand drone capabilities within the Canadian Armed Forces and Coast Guard. Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has committed to increasing defence spending, with Canada meeting NATO's two percent of GDP target this year and working towards a new target of five percent by 2035.
